purpose: One golden input per AttentionSignalKind. tests/harden-notify-fixtures.test.ts runs each row through detectAttentionSignal so a rewritten detector cannot silently invent a kind, drop a silent kind, or reclassify a person-blocker as a watcher notice. Absence of attentionClass on the three silent kinds is a case, not a gap — the notification center must never invent a third severity for them.

cases.name: permission-requested — control-plane permission is a person-blocker
cases.claim: A cmux permission prompt means a human is the blocker. Delivery, the ember badge, and the center's Waiting-on-you verdict all depend on this kind staying blocking — never demoted to a watcher notice, never recoverable from agent-authored transcript text.

input.attentionNotification: Claude needs your permission to run git push

expect.nextAction: Approve or deny the permission it is blocked on.
expect.evidence: Claude needs your permission to run git push

cases.name: input-requested — control-plane wait without naming a permission
cases.claim: cmux can say the agent is waiting without naming a permission. That is still a person-blocker (blocking), not a weaker advisory — the operator is the reason it stopped.

input.attentionNotification: Claude is waiting for your input

expect.nextAction: Answer it: cmux reports it is waiting on you.
expect.evidence: Claude is waiting for your input

cases.name: fork-unresolved — named alternatives handed back
cases.claim: Two named options with the choice handed back is a fork, not a generic question. The center must surface a pick-one action, and the kind must stay in the blocking set so an out-of-page notification still fires.

input.lastAgentClosing: I can either widen the lock or shard the writer queue. Which would you prefer?

expect.nextAction: Pick one of the options it stopped between.

cases.name: handoff-stated — declarative hand-back without a question mark
cases.claim: Most real waits end in a statement, not a question. If handoff-stated ever falls out of blocking, the center goes quiet on the common case the question detector is structurally blind to.

expect.nextAction: Take the decision it handed back.

cases.name: question-pending — agent stopped on an interrogative
cases.claim: A closing interrogative is the classic ask. It must remain blocking so badge ink, OS delivery, and the live feed agree that a person is the blocker.

input.lastAgentClosing: Do you want me to land this now?

expect.nextAction: Answer the question it stopped on.
expect.evidence: Do you want me to land this now?

cases.name: assumption-stated — proceeded on a stated assumption
cases.claim: An agent that names the assumption it proceeded on invited correction. That is still a person-blocker: silence from the operator is consent by omission, so the center must keep it blocking.

input.lastAgentMessage: The spec is ambiguous about retries. I will assume three attempts with backoff unless you say otherwise. Moving on to the writer.

expect.nextAction: Confirm or correct the assumption it proceeded on.

cases.name: stalled-active — watcher noticed, person is not the blocker
cases.claim: A manifest-active lane whose hook stayed idle too long is something the board noticed — not something a person is blocking. attentionClass is noticed (amber outline, no OS notification). Collapsing this into blocking would lie at the one place the operator cannot see the screen to check.

expect.evidence: Hook idle for 31 minutes; manifest declares active.

cases.name: nothing-wanted — we read its closing words and nothing wants you
cases.claim: Readable closing text that asks nothing is a finding: we looked. It must carry NO attentionClass — absence, not a third severity — or the center will invent work from an honest quiet.

input.lastAgentClosing: All tests pass and it is committed.

cases.name: out-of-scope — ended session cannot be answered
cases.claim: An ended row has every control disabled. Surfacing it as blocking or noticed would put a to-do on a corpse. No attentionClass; never enters the live center.

input.lastAgentMessage: No security vulnerabilities identified in this diff.

cases.name: not-readable — nothing to read is not all-clear
cases.claim: Blind silence is the opposite of an honest quiet. Counting it as nothing-wanted made a blind layer look disciplined. No attentionClass, and never a correct-negative on the board.
